jobs.title: Staff AI Engineer, Developer Relations Engineering
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is hiring an AI Engineer for our Developer Relations Engineering team: an engineer who builds agentic AI systems and enjoys showing other developers how they work. You will build reference agents, open-source integrations, and sample applications on Crusoe Cloud and Crusoe Managed Inference.

In this role, you will lead technical content creation, community engagement, and developer outreach across AI infrastructure and managed services workloads. You will produce documentation, tutorials, white papers, sample applications, and video guides.

You will partner with the Product, Engineering, Research, and GTM/Solutions Engineering teams and work across the open-source agent ecosystem.

You will spend most of your time building and then sharing what you build.

What You'll Be Working On:

Agentic Reference Systems: Architect and ship end-to-end reference agents and starter kits on Crusoe that developers can use as a starting point for production, covering tool use, MCP, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, structured outputs, memory, and evals.
Examples & Documentation: Own the code examples, tutorials, and documentation that help developers go from first API call to working agent, and keep them tested and up to date as the ecosystem changes.
Open Source & GitHub: Own Crusoe's developer-facing GitHub presence, including examples, cookbooks, and integrations. Contribute upstream to agent frameworks, inference engines, and developer tooling (for example LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP, vLLM, and SGLang) so they work well with Crusoe.
Technical Content & Video: Turn the systems you build into content developers rely on: deep-dive blog posts, notebooks, YouTube videos, livestreams, and short technical clips.
Building in Public: Share your work on X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Discord, Reddit, Hacker News, etc. Answer technical questions, review community projects, and become a trusted technical voice in the agent and open-source community.
Use-Case Blueprints: Partner with GTM/Solutions Engineering to spot recurring customer patterns and turn them into open reference architectures for developer segments such as Physical AI, robotics, simulation, and other industry verticals.
Product & Research Partnership: Join Product, Engineering, and Research workflows. Test features and models before launch, make sure samples and docs are ready on launch day, and bring developer friction back as concrete product input, following each issue until it is fixed or explicitly deprioritized.
Talks & Workshops: Give technical talks, live demos, and hands-on labs at conferences, meetups, hackathons, and workshops.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Engineering Experience: 5+ years as a software engineer, ML engineer, applied AI engineer, forward-deployed engineer, or in a similar hands-on engineering role, with strong Python. A Developer Relations title is not required.
Engineering Credibility: Ability to earn credibility with both AI infrastructure engineers and ML/AI engineers.
Agentic AI: Hands-on experience building LLM applications and agents with tool calling, MCP, retrieval, memory, and evaluation, using one or more frameworks such as LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, or the OpenAI Agents SDK. You have well-formed opinions about what works and what breaks in production.
Cloud Infrastructure: Experience working with cloud computing platforms (such as AWS, GCP, or Azure) or managed AI solutions, with a foundational understanding of cloud infrastructure concepts.
Inference & Model Serving: Working knowledge of how models are served, including OpenAI-compatible APIs, open-weight models, and serving engines such as vLLM or SGLang. You can explain cost and latency tradeoffs credibly.

About The Role

The Growth team's job is to keep Anthropic on the exponential by getting more people and companies using and paying for Claude. Growth Data Scientists partner closely with growth product managers, engineers and marketers on experimentation, opportunity sizing, strategic analysis, metrics and personalization.

About

We're hiring for two focus areas within this posting. Tell us in your application which one fits you best, or if you're excited about both:

Growth generalist: a strong generalist across marketing and product who drives experimentation, opportunity sizing, marketing measurement and strategic analysis.
Personalization: building and evaluating the models and experiments that pick the right message, offer or product experience for each user, across lifecycle marketing, onboarding and in-product experiences.

We work in an AI-native way. Much of our analysis, reporting and experiment work is done with Claude as a collaborator, and we expect you to push that further.

Responsibilities

Across both focus areas, you will:

Design and analyze A/B tests and quasi-experiments across activation, retention and monetization, and turn the results into a clear call on what to ship
Define systems of metrics and guardrails that tie short-term wins to long-term value
Present analyses and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences, leading with the decision and keeping the numbers in support

In The Growth Generalist Focus, You Will Also

Size opportunities and make the case for what Growth should work on next
Measure the incrementality of paid and lifecycle marketing with holdouts, geo experiments and other causal methods, and turn the results into budget and channel recommendations
Tie acquisition and lifecycle programs to long-term value (LTV, CAC and payback)

In The Personalization Focus, You Will Also

Build and ship targeting and personalization models that decide which users get which message, offer or experience, working closely with growth product managers and engineers
Design the tests that evaluate and iterate on our personalization strategy, including holdouts, bandits and off-policy estimates where A/B tests aren't practical

You may be a good fit if you have

7+ years of experience in data science, with significant time on growth, marketing, lifecycle or personalization problems
Deep expertise in experimental design and causal inference, including A/B testing at scale, holdouts and quasi-experimental methods when randomization isn't available
Experience analyzing growth funnels: acquisition, activation, retention and monetization
Proficiency with Python and SQL
Clear written communication, and a track record of recommendations that changed priorities or what a team built
A bias for action and comfort in ambiguous, fast-moving environments
An interest in Anthropic's mission of building safe and beneficial AI

For The Growth Generalist Focus, We're Also Looking For

Experience measuring marketing: incrementality testing, holdouts or geo experiments, and LTV/CAC for paid or lifecycle programs

For The Personalization Focus, We're Also Looking For

Hands-on experience building and shipping machine learning models that drive user-facing decisions (targeting, ranking, recommendation or personalization)

Strong candidates may also have

Experience defining activation metrics and lifecycle measurement for a product-led business
Experience with experimentation platforms and meta-analysis across experiment portfolios
Background at consumption-based, multi-product companies serving both consumers and enterprises

Experience with lifecycle or CRM personalization (email, push, in-product messaging) and its measurement problems, such as global holdouts and interference between campaigns

About Veeco

You probably don’t realize it, but what we do at Veeco touches the lives of every person, every day. It’s a bold statement, but it’s true. From the smartphones in our pockets that access the world’s collective knowledge, to the cloud-based services where all that information lives, to high-speed wireless communication and computing power needed to drive artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality, gaming and so much more, our technology is all around us.

We design, develop, manufacture, and service highly complex, cutting-edge machines used by our customers to create the essential devices that drive the digital age, connect the world, and improve the human experience. Along with the world’s leading technology companies, many of which are household names, we help solve their most difficult material science challenges, enabling technologies for a more connected, sustainable, and convenient world.

We’re looking for material difference-makers to join our growing team. Interested? Learn more at www.veeco.com/careers .

Overview

Improving the performance, reliability, and manufacturability of laser spike annealing systems requires deep expertise across applied physics, high-power lasers, optical measurement, and optomechanical design. As a Senior Research Scientist, you will turn complex technical and customer challenges into validated system and subsystem solutions, from early concept through prototype testing and product transition. Your work will strengthen Veeco's laser-based semiconductor processing technology by expanding system capability, resolving critical performance issues, and improving customer outcomes. You will shape experiments, design decisions, and technical roadmaps while working across optical, electrical, mechanical, product marketing, and technical support teams.

Lead the design and validation of laser spike annealing system and subsystem improvements that advance performance, reliability, and product capability.
Translate complex engineering and customer problems into experimental plans, technical requirements, risk assessments, and clear development recommendations.
Design, integrate, and test prototypes, assemblies, optical diagnostics, and optomechanical components from concept through verification.
Own laboratory experiments and data analysis, using results to identify root causes, guide design decisions, and define next-step development work.
Diagnose precision-system performance issues across optical, electrical, mechanical, software, and process interfaces, then drive solutions with cross-functional partners.
Convert customer needs and field findings into technology development and transition plans that align research, product, and service teams.
Serve as a technical resource for customers, suppliers, and strategic partners, communicating findings and recommendations with clarity and sound technical judgment.

Qualifications

Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in physics, applied physics, optical engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field, plus at least three years of relevant industry or applied research experience or a Master’s degree and six years of experience is required. Hands-on experience with high-power laser systems, optical measurement, laboratory prototyping, and precision-system testing is also required.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Deep knowledge of laser physics, optical systems, optomechanical components, measurement methods, and laboratory safety practices.
Skilled at designing experiments, analyzing incomplete or complex data, and converting results into defensible engineering decisions.
Proficient in precision-system troubleshooting, including isolating interactions among hardware, software, controls, optics, and process conditions.
Experienced with design and analysis tools used for optical, mechanical, system, or experimental development.
Able to distill complex technical findings into clear written summaries, design reviews, and recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.
Effective at guiding cross-functional work across research, engineering, product marketing, technical support, customers, and suppliers without direct authority.
Knowledge of semiconductor fabrication, thermal processing, or capital equipment development is preferred.
Experience using programming for instrument control, data acquisition, automation, or technical analysis.
Ability to travel internationally up to 30% and work for extended periods in a Class 1000 cleanroom environment.

recruiting@veeco.com .

Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Time

Commuter Benefits
Life and Accident Insurance
Disability Insurance

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

When you see what modern language models are capable of, do you wonder, "How do these things work? How can we trust them?"

The Interpretability team at Anthropic is working to reverse-engineer how trained models work because we believe that a mechanistic understanding is the most robust way to make advanced systems safe. We’re looking for researchers and engineers to join our efforts.

People mean many different things by "interpretability". We're focused on mechanistic interpretability, which aims to discover how neural network parameters map to meaningful algorithms. Some useful analogies might be to think of us as trying to do "biology" or "neuroscience" of neural networks using “microscopes” we build, or as treating neural networks as binary computer programs we're trying to "reverse engineer".

A few places to learn more about our work and team at a high level are this introduction to Interpretability from our research lead, Chris Olah; a discussion of our work on the Hard Fork podcast produced by the New York Times, and this blog post (and accompanying video) sharing more about some of the engineering challenges we’d had to solve to get these results. Some of our team's notable publications include A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits, In-context Learning and Induction Heads, Toy Models of Superposition, Scaling Monosemanticity, and our Circuits’ Methods and Biology papers. This work builds on ideas from members' work prior to Anthropic such as the original circuits thread, Multimodal Neurons, Activation Atlases, and Building Blocks.

We aim to create a solid foundation for mechanistically understanding neural networks and making them safe (see our vision post). In the short term, we have focused on resolving the issue of "superposition" (see Toy Models of Superposition, Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent, and our May 2023 update), which causes the computational units of the models, like neurons and attention heads, to be individually uninterpretable, and on finding ways to decompose models into more interpretable components. Our subsequent work found millions of features in Sonnet, one of our production language models, represents progress in this direction. In our most recent work, we develop methods that allow us to build circuits using features and use this circuits to understand the mechanisms associated with a model's computation and study specific examples of multi-hop reasoning, planning, and chain-of-thought faithfulness on Haiku 3.5, one of our production models.” This is a stepping stone towards our overall goal of mechanistically understanding neural networks.

We often collaborate with teams across Anthropic, such as Alignment Science and Societal Impacts to use our work to make Anthropic’s models safer. We also have an Interpretability Architectures project that involves collaborating with Pretraining.

Develop methods for understanding LLMs by reverse engineering algorithms learned in their weights
Design and run robust experiments, both quickly in toy scenarios and at scale in large models
Create and analyze new interpretability features and circuits to better understand how models work.
Build infrastructure for running experiments and visualizing results
Work with colleagues to communicate results internally and publicly

You can clearly articulate and discuss the motivations behind your work, and teach us about what you've learned. You like writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Global GTM Operations team is responsible for overall productivity and effectiveness of the GTM organization, partnering closely with the sales team and teams across Stripe to drive initiatives. This role will partner directly with the head of the global Solution Architecture, whose team is responsible for pre-sales technical assessment and technical validation of Users in partnership with Sales. This role will be expected to drive the rhythm of business, data insights / reporting, strategic initiatives, annual planning and execution. We advance the sales policies, processes and tools to drive revenue and growth.

This is an incredible opportunity that plays an integral role in shaping and executing GTM strategies with Sales leaders. Responsibilities include go-to-market design, resource planning, territory alignment and quotas management, sales process optimization, and business analytics. You will also partner with key cross-functional stakeholders, including Finance & Strategy, adjacent Sales Operations teams, Global Systems & Processes, and the Strategy Planning and Insights team to streamline and optimize our internal processes and deliverables (monthly business reviews, weekly forecasting calls, target setting and planning). We are looking for a self-starter who is passionate about their work, detail oriented, analytical and has demonstrated success dealing with ambiguity in a high-growth environment, and solving problems with limited oversight.

What you’ll do

The Solution Architecture team is growing rapidly and is in need of a strong strategy and ops business partner that can help scale the operations and drive strategy of the team. This entails a focus on operational projects (process design, business cadences, systems work) and everything related to planning and running their business, including: org design and planning, sales coverage models, setting SOKRs, measuring and providing insights on performance, and process improvement. In addition to engaging with the Solutions Architecture team, you will also be collaborating with numerous cross-functional stakeholders from across the globe.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solution Architecture leadership and cross-functional stakeholders in developing go-to market strategy, resource plan and key performance metrics.
Create and manage operational processes such as territory planning, quota setting, quarterly compensation.
Work cross-functionally to investigate and conduct analysis on system and operational issues
Develop and execute initiatives designed to optimize team efficiency and productivity
Drive rhythm of business (weekly business reviews, monthly / quarterly business reviews) with strong operational rigor.
Provide insights on key performance metrics and priorities (e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly business reviews), identify key roadblocks to progress, and work efficiently to remove them
Provide business analytic strength to help drive initiatives critical to ongoing growth and provide key insights for business leadership to support strategic decision-making
Drive critical projects and initiatives and drive alignment with cross-functional teams across the organization by developing detailed project plans with activity based milestones
Oversee implementation of enabling systems and tools, working closely with internal systems teams

Who you are

X is a diverse group of inventors and entrepreneurs who build and launch technologies that aim to improve the lives of millions, even billions, of people. Our team – Bellwether – operates at the intersection of machine learning, geospatial data, and pressing issues with enterprise customers, governments, and more. We focus on severe weather manifestations of climate change, such as wildfires, and aim to use a wide range of data and analytics to better understand and predict what these events could mean for communities and businesses across the globe. We do this through the detection and classification of the features and patterns of the natural and built worlds, the application of cutting-edge machine learning, and the redesign of the full geo-ML workflow. We're looking for an experienced ML engineer with a strong background in ML in production and MLOps framework for enabling continual learning. jobs.title: Principal AI Ops Engineer
jobs.description:
Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

What You'll Do

You will build the systems that let AI agents, not people, do most of the work of running Crux's TPU fleet. Reporting to our Director, AI Ops, you will be one of the first engineers on the team, writing the telemetry pipelines, correlation logic, and agents that detect, triage, and remediate failures across facilities, TPU hosts, the network, and the control plane before a customer notices. You will turn every runbook into code and every repeat incident into automation. This is a hands-on engineering seat: you write and ship the software, then operate it in production.

In This Role, You Will

Build and own the telemetry and event pipeline that ties together power, cooling, TPU hosts, interconnect, and the control plane, with the correlation to tell a failing pump from a failing chip from a failing job.
Write AI agents that triage alerts, execute runbooks, drain and requeue workloads, and open hardware repair and RMA requests with Google, with every action logged, reversible, and measured.
Turn runbooks into code, so that every critical failure mode for the first build maps to a signal, an alert, an automated response, and an owner.
Build the guardrails that keep autonomous actions safe: blast-radius limits, approval gates for high-risk changes, and tested rollback paths.
Define and instrument SLOs and error budgets with Compute, Network Engineering, and Facility Operations, and build the views the team reviews every week.
Take part in on-call and incident response, and drive postmortems that end in a fix that ships, not an action item that ages.
Measure the share of operational work that closes with zero human touch, and drive that number up release over release.

SIGNALS OF SUCCESS

After 60 Days In This Role

Gained a complete understanding of the first-build architecture, the failure modes that matter most, and the tooling in place today, and shipped a first working agent against a real, repeat failure.
Stood up the first version of the unified telemetry pipeline for the first build.
Adapted to a fast-paced environment, triaging appropriately and continuously improving our function.

After 6 Months

Taken the first Stage 1 cluster into production with automated detection and remediation in place for its top failure modes.
Shipped agents the team relies on every day, with a measured share of incidents resolved without human intervention.
Built the guardrails and audit trail that let the team trust autonomous actions in production.

After 1 Year

Running automation across a multi-site fleet where most repeat operational work executes autonomously, with measurable gains in availability, recovery time, and cost per chip.
Built a library of agents and runbooks-as-code that every new site inherits on day one.
Become a reason strong SRE and operations engineers choose Crux.

Experiences

EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH

10+ years in software engineering, SRE, or production engineering for large-scale infrastructure, including operating a fleet across many sites against hard SLAs.
Built and shipped AI-driven operations systems in production, such as event correlation, anomaly detection, auto-remediation, or agentic triage, with measurable results.
Strong software skills in Python or Go, and hands-on experience with observability stacks (for example Prometheus or OpenTelemetry), Kubernetes, and large-scale data pipelines.

Attributes

You are outcome driven and hands-on. You read the telemetry and write the agent yourself. This is a builder's seat, not a supervisory one.
You are close enough to the hardware to be useful. You understand how power, cooling, accelerators, and networks fail, not just how software does.
You have a high tolerance for ambiguity. You absorb ambiguity and navigate complexity rather than passing it along.

Mindset

You are skeptical by default. "90% automated" is a hypothesis until it survives a bad night at a new site. You build the system that makes the next incident boring.
You deliver reliability through discipline, not heroics. You would rather fix the cause once than page someone twice.
You are AI-agentic first. Fluent with AI agents, or committed to becoming so quickly, you embed them as first principles in how you and your team work, defaulting to agentic workflows before adding headcount or process.

Nice To Have (Preferred, Not Required)

SRE or production engineering at a hyperscaler (Google, Meta, Microsoft, AWS) or a neocloud (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe).
Experience operating TPU or GPU clusters for large training and inference workloads, including hardware health, repair workflows, and fleet telemetry.
Experience with data center infrastructure telemetry such as BMS, DCIM, or power and cooling systems.
Experience building LLM-based agents with tool use, evaluations, and safety controls in production.
Experience with predictive maintenance, ML-based anomaly detection, or failure prediction at fleet scale.

Company-paid life insurance and disability
Full suite of other optional benefits
401(k) Plan with 4% company match
Hybrid schedule offering four days in-office collaboration paired with one remote workday for focused, individual work

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About The Role

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it. The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity.

We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security. Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other.

Key responsibilities

Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on
Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed
Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them
Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on
Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing
Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance
Write clear design documents for what you build

Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go

Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30.

Anthropic Fellows Program Overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output
(e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

What To Expect

4 months of full-time research
Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
Access to a shared workspace (in either Berkeley, California or London, UK)
Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community
Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

Across the workstreams, you may be a good fit if you:

Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
Are excited to transition into empirical AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic
Have a strong technical background in computer science, mathematics, or physics
Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong Candidates May Also Have

Strong background in a discipline relevant to a specific Fellows workstream (e.g. economics, social sciences, or cybersecurity)
Experience in areas of research or engineering related to their workstream

Candidates Must Be

Fluent in Python programming
Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

AI Safety Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

Sam Bowman
Sara Price
Alex Tamkin
Nina Panickssery
Trenton Bricken
Logan Graham
Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
Joe Benton
Collin Burns
Fabien Roger
Samuel Marks
Kyle Fish
Ethan Perez

Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as:

Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about past projects, including:

Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data: Alex Cloud and Minh Le, et al., mentors including Samuel Marks and Owain Evans
Open-source circuits: Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey

For a full list of representative projects for each area, please see these blog posts: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research, Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions.

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
Have experience with empirical ML research projects
Have experience working with large language models
Have experience in one of the research areas mentioned above
Have a track record of open-source contributions

AI Security Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

Nicholas Carlini
Keri Warr
Evyatar Ben Asher
Keane Lucas
Newton Cheng

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about some past Fellows projects, including:

AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits: Winnie Xiao and Cole Killian, mentored by Nicholas Carlini and Alwin Peng
Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations: Chloe Loughridge et al., mentored by Jon Kutasov and Joe Benton

Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
Have contributed to open-source projects in LLM- or security-adjacent repositories
Have demonstrated success in bringing clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems
Have experience with pentesting, vulnerability research, or other offensive security work
Have a demonstrated willingness to do the "dirty work" that produces high-quality outputs
Have reported CVEs or been awarded bug bounties
Have experience with empirical ML research projects
Have experience with deep learning frameworks and experiment management

To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.

currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.

Be the DRI for scientific enablement: decide what to run, build the materials, deliver them, and measure whether research teams reach daily use of Claude.

Scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic: train our Applied AI and Customer Success teams, and build playbooks they can run without you.
Build and lead a scientist community around Claude, and be its ambassador (and support ambassador programs), from small meetups to large conferences.

jobs.title: Senior Principal AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Our Engineering organization is scaling its AI Engineering capabilities under new leadership, creating an opportunity to shape the next generation of AI at Rapid7. We’re looking for Senior Principal AI Engineers to define and influence the technical direction of our LLM and agentic AI systems across the organization. You’ll tackle our most complex technical challenges, establish architectural principles and engineering standards, and drive greenfield innovation that delivers meaningful impact for our global customers. Through technical leadership and mentoring, you’ll shape strategic product and platform investments and influence how we build and scale AI across Rapid7.

About The Team

AI is reshaping cybersecurity on both sides. Attackers can use AI to strike at machine speed, and only AI-powered defense can keep up. At the same time, organizations can only adopt AI with confidence if it is secure. Rapid7 sits at the intersection of security and AI, and we are building industry-defining products for this new era.

Rapid7's AI Engineering team builds the AI that powers our security platform. We are AI engineers and applied scientists who take models from research to production, combining open-source and frontier LLMs, AI agents, and fast predictive models with more than 20 years of Rapid7 security expertise. Our work drives core use cases across Detection and Response, such as alert triage, threat investigation, and automated response, and Exposure and Remediation, such as vulnerability prioritization, attack surface risk assessment, and guided remediation. Together, these help customers stop threats faster and fix what matters most.

About The Role

As a Senior Principal AI Engineer, you will set the technical direction for how Rapid7 builds, tunes and serves LLMs and agentic systems across its security products. You understand LLMs from the ground up, from transformer internals and training to fine-tuning and inference optimization, and you stay hands-on with the hardest problems. You know where LLMs shine and where they fall short, and you treat them as one tool in the AI toolbox, alongside predictive AI and classical ML, choosing the right approach for each problem. Specifically your focus will be to:

Set the AI technical vision, architecture and multi-year roadmap for LLM and agentic systems across Detection and Response and Exposure and Remediation
Define company-wide model strategy, including when to use frontier or open-source models, when to fine-tune, distill or post-train, and where to invest in new capabilities
Lead the most complex and highest-risk technical initiatives across multiple teams, including fine-tuning, distillation and post-training of open-source LLMs on security data
Establish company-wide standards for context engineering, inference optimization and evaluation, with evals as the release gate for every AI system we ship
Lead optimization of LLM inference at scale, balancing quality, latency and cost
Lead design reviews, resolve the most complex technical trade-offs, and stay hands-on by prototyping and building critical model, training and inference code

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data scientists and data analysts learn and grow together. The Treasury Finance Data Science team builds the models, risk frameworks, and decision tools behind how Stripe manages money at global scale: liquidity, funding, counterparty risk, and foreign exchange.

Stripe moves funds across 135+ currencies every day. That creates FX exposure from merchant flows, multi-currency balances, and entity funding. In this role, you'll be a thought partner and builder alongside Stripe's FX team. Together you'll develop the quantitative foundation for how Stripe measures, forecasts, and hedges FX exposure.

What you'll do

You'll be the senior quantitative lead for FX within Treasury Finance Data Science. You'll co-build with Treasury, the FX hedging team, Finance, and Engineering: shaping the research agenda, turning ideas into rigorous models, and building the systems that put those models to work. Data Science owns these systems. They produce the decision-critical outputs and analyses that the FX team and Treasury leadership rely on. This is a hands-on role. You'll design the methodology, write the code, and ship it into production.

Responsibilities

Partner with the FX team to build and evolve FX risk measurement: exposure aggregation across entities and currencies, VaR / Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis
Develop forecasting models for FX exposures and multi-currency cash flows. Quantify forecast uncertainty so it can inform hedge sizing and timing.
Co-design hedge optimization and decision frameworks with the FX team that weigh hedge cost, residual risk, P&L volatility, and liquidity constraints
Build ML and statistical systems for trading and risk (signal research, anomaly detection on flows, execution and cost analytics), and take them from prototype to production
Own the production systems that generate decision-critical FX outputs, partnering with Engineering on reliability, SLAs, monitoring, alerting, and incident response for risk-critical workflows
Partner deeply with Treasury Finance stakeholders to turn business questions into quantitative frameworks. Anticipate needs and help shape FX risk strategy rather than reacting to requests.
Produce clear, trusted analyses and reporting that inform Treasury and Finance leadership decisions, including leadership-level reporting such as MBRs and QBRs
Use AI tools (code assistants, LLM-based agents) to speed up modeling, analysis, and automation, while maintaining rigor, validation, and auditability
Raise the technical bar for FX quantitative work within Data Science: methodology standards, model validation, documentation, and mentoring other data scientists

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Location Requirement

New York, NY required (50% in office - hybrid)

Minimum Requirements

PhD with 1-3 years, MS or MA with 2-6 years, or BS or BA with 4-8 years of data science or quantitative modeling experience
Hands-on quantitative experience at a bank, asset manager, hedge fund, trading firm, or similar financial institution, with direct exposure to FX, rates, or market risk
Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and time-series modeling, plus working knowledge of risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress testing) and hedging instruments (forwards, swaps, options)
Proficiency in Python and SQL. You write production-quality code, not just research scripts.
Experience taking models or analytical systems from research into production
Business acumen and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, decision-ready insights
Ability to clearly communicate results and drive impact with cross-functional partners, including senior non-technical stakeholders
Ability to manage multiple projects at once, with strong attention to detail
Experience using AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis, and coding

Preferred Qualifications

Degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative / Mathematical Finance, Financial Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research)
Applied machine learning experience in trading or risk (e.g., forecasting, execution analytics, signal research, anomaly detection)
Experience with corporate treasury or balance-sheet FX: multi-entity exposure management, hedge programs, and treasury concepts such as liquidity, funding, and cash positioning
Experience building risk or decision systems with engineering standards: code review, testing, monitoring, and defined SLAs
Experience with distributed data tools (e.g., Spark) and workflow orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Flyte)
Prior experience at a growth-stage internet, fintech, or payments company
Experience creating leadership-level reporting, such as QBRs and MBRs
A builder's mindset, with a willingness to question assumptions and conventional wisdom
Interest in how data products enable automated and agentic workflows, and an understanding that model and data quality determine the reliability of every downstream decision

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $159,000 - $288,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. We help protect our customers against life’s uncertainties. Regardless of where you work within the company, you’ll be helping provide protection and peace of mind when our customers need it most.

The Data Solutions Architect is a senior individual contributor who serves as a bridge between business strategy and technical execution, designing end‑to‑end data solutions that enable analytics, reporting, and AI use cases across the enterprise. This role combines deep data architecture expertise with solution design and technical leadership responsibilities—creating practical, scalable, and secure data solutions that translate business needs into actionable technical roadmaps.

This position is embedded closer to delivery teams, working hands‑on with business partners, engineers, and product teams to ensure data solutions are usable, compliant, and aligned to Protective’s priorities.

While this role has no direct reports, it carries significant leadership accountability. The Data Solutions Architect is expected to set technical direction, drive alignment across independent teams, and influence outcomes through expertise, credibility, and relationships rather than positional authority. Decisions made in this role shape multi‑year data investments, establish patterns adopted by multiple engineering teams, and directly affect Protective’s ability to deliver trusted data and AI capabilities at scale.

Scope and Level of Influence

Individual contributor role with enterprise‑level impact; leads through influence, not through direct reporting relationships.
Serves as the recognized design authority for assigned data domains and initiatives, with the standing to approve, challenge, or redirect solution designs.
Operates with a high degree of autonomy on ambiguous, cross‑domain problems where requirements, ownership, and precedent are not yet established.
Sets direction that is adopted by multiple delivery teams and persists well beyond the life of any single project.
Escalates and resolves architectural disagreements across teams, bringing stakeholders to a defensible, documented decision.
Trusted to represent the data organization in enterprise forums, executive conversations, and vendor or partner discussions.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership and Direction

Set and communicate the technical direction for data solutions across assigned domains, establishing the patterns, standards, and reference designs that other teams build against.
Serve as design authority for significant data initiatives—reviewing, approving, and where necessary challenging designs proposed by delivery teams.
Drive alignment across teams with competing priorities, differing technical opinions, and separate reporting lines, building consensus where possible and making clear recommendations where consensus is not reachable.
Make and defend architectural decisions under uncertainty, documenting rationale, trade‑offs, and the conditions under which a decision should be revisited.
Anticipate downstream technical and organizational consequences of design choices, and proactively raise risks before they become delivery problems.
Represent data architecture positions credibly to senior technology and business leadership.

Data and System Solution Design

Design and implement end‑to‑end data solutions, including data warehouses, data lakes, and data pipelines, to support analytics, reporting, and AI initiatives.
Define logical and physical data models that balance business usability with technical efficiency.
Select and apply appropriate technologies (cloud platforms, database engines, orchestration tools) based on use case, scale, and cost considerations.

Business and Technical Translation

Partner with business stakeholders and leaders to understand objectives and translate them into clear technical requirements for data, reporting, and advanced analytics.
Frame technical options as business decisions—articulating cost, risk, time‑to‑value, and long‑term implications so leaders can choose with confidence.
Influence business stakeholders toward sustainable solutions, including the ability to constructively push back on requests that create long‑term cost, risk, or complexity.
Ensure data solutions support accuracy, accessibility, governance, and regulatory compliance.
Act as a design authority during delivery, ensuring solutions meet business intent while remaining technically sound.

Data Integration and Enablement

Design integration patterns to move and share data across systems using APIs, services, and pipelines.
Enable downstream consumption by analytics, BI, and AI platforms through well‑structured, well‑documented data products.
Reduce point‑to‑point integrations by promoting reusable, scalable data patterns and driving their adoption across teams.

Strategic Data Planning

Shape and influence multi‑year data roadmaps that prioritize high‑value use cases while avoiding data redundancy and unmanaged “data swamps.”
Partner with platform, governance, and enterprise architecture teams to align solution designs with enterprise standards and capabilities—and to evolve those standards where they no longer serve the business.
Identify opportunities to simplify, consolidate, or modernize existing data solutions, and build the business case needed to fund and sequence that work.
Advise leadership on build‑versus‑buy decisions, platform selection, and the architectural implications of strategic investments.

Security, Scalability, and Reliability

Ensure solutions scale to support increasing data volumes, complexity, and business demand.
Incorporate resiliency, monitoring, and operational considerations into solution designs.

Mentorship and Capability Building

Mentor data engineers and less experienced architects, raising the overall design and technical judgment of the data organization.
Lead design reviews and architecture working sessions that develop others while improving outcomes.
Create durable artifacts—reference architectures, design patterns, decision records, and documentation—that scale the architect’s judgment beyond their personal involvement.

Strong understanding of modern data architectures, including data lakes, data warehouses, and streaming or batch pipelines.

Ability to translate business problems into practical technical designs without over‑engineering.

jobs.title: Staff Research Engineer, Multi-Agent Scaling
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Large teams of agents are starting to solve problems no single agent can, from rewriting major codebases to formalizing landmark mathematics. Our team studies how these teams scale: what happens to performance, cost and coordination as the number of agents, the compute budget and the length of the task grow, and what has to change to keep getting returns from that scale. We build the platform and evaluations Anthropic uses to run and measure large agent teams, and other research teams build on them.

This role lives at the boundary between research and engineering. It is a generalist role on a small team: you'll design and run large experiments, build the systems they run on, and get to the bottom of surprising results. We often need to go from a vague question to a running experiment quickly.

Responsibilities

Design, run and interpret large-scale experiments on agent teams, reasoning rigorously about what the data does and doesn't show
Investigate how performance and efficiency change as team size, compute and task horizon grow, and find the bottlenecks that limit them
Build and scale the systems that run very large agent teams reliably, and debug the failures that only appear at scale
Design evaluations for long-horizon problems, and keep their results trustworthy
Build the tooling and metrics that let researchers see what a large agent team is doing and why
Partner with research teams across Anthropic so they can run their own experiments on the platform, and communicate findings clearly

You May Be a Good Fit If You

Have significant software engineering, ML or research engineering experience
Have owned something substantial end to end, such as a large system, an evaluation or benchmark, an agent product, or a research project
Genuinely enjoy both research and engineering work
Think quantitatively about complex systems, and think twice before trusting a number
Can work from a vague question rather than a spec
Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Have clear written and verbal communication
Care about the societal impacts of your work

Strong Candidates May Also Have

Experience building or operating large-scale distributed systems, such as schedulers, sandboxed code execution, or inference and RL infrastructure
Built evaluations, benchmarks or harnesses for LLMs or agents
Experience building complex agentic systems that use LLMs
Experience with scaling laws or other large-scale empirical research
A background in operations research, statistics, economics, physics, quantitative finance, or another field that models and optimizes complex systems

Strong Candidates Need Not Have

Formal certifications or education credentials
Academic research experience or publication history
Prior experience with multi-agent systems or reinforcement learning

Representative Projects

Measure how performance scales with the number of agents on a hard problem, and explain where the curve bends and why
Prepare our largest-ever agent run: find what breaks as team size and task length grow together, and fix it before launch
Work out how to allocate a fixed compute budget across a team of agents to solve a problem fastest
Build tooling that turns the activity of a large agent team into something a researcher can read in minutes
Design a novel eval that distinguishes real gains in teamwork from artifacts of the evaluation setup

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.

Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. As an AI-native company, we believe technology should expand the reach, quality, and humanity of care. Every Spring Health team member is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully, apply human judgment to AI outputs, and keep building AI fluency in ways that support their role and our mission.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Engineering, AI Tooling & Enablement, this Staff Software Engineer will lead architecture and technical strategy for AI transformation. You will translate broad product and organizational visions into scalable, modular system architectures, and act as a critical partner to Product, Engineering, and cross-functional leaders to build scalable, future-proof platform capabilities with speed, quality, and precision. This role is part of the AI Transformation & Platform Engineering team and is instrumental in modernizing our technologies through AI-driven capabilities spanning UI, harnesses, models, connectors, and governance accelerating delivery and business impact across the org.

Please note that this is a hybrid role based in New York City
, with an expectation to be in the office 2–3 days per week at our 60 Madison Avenue location. Candidates must be based in the NYC metro area or able to relocate independently within 90 days of their start date. Occasional travel will be required for team on-sites.

Lead hands-on experimentation, evaluation, and production rollout of modern AI capabilities, frameworks, and workflows (LLMs, model gateways, retrieval systems) across the engineering & enterprise platforms
Identify recurring systemic breakdowns in the software development lifecycle and design simpler, faster, higher-quality approaches to raise the bar for code quality, system resilience, and operational health

Drive best practices across the organization; lead initiatives to eliminate tech debt and prepare the codebase for future roadmap requirements.
Critically influence large, cross-team projects—ensuring execution without delay or compromise, and anticipating and removing barriers of all kinds.
Bring critical thinking and drive shared understanding in ambiguous situations; given a clear vision, create a strategy; given a clear strategy, define a sequence of objectives.
Provide a system-wide view to the engineers you work with; share architectural improvements across the tech org to build buy-in and drive broad implementation.
Develop strong working relationships cross-functionally and with business stakeholders; make sound tradeoffs between competing needs across short- and long-term horizons.
Empower engineers to set ambitious goals and turn vision into reality; mentor and develop engineers across the organization, not just your immediate team.

About Arketa

Arketa is building the operating system for modern fitness and wellness. Our mission is to make wellness more accessible by empowering studios and wellness entrepreneurs to grow beyond in-person classes. We provide a powerful, all-in-one platform to manage and scale hybrid wellness businesses, whether online, in-person, or both.

With Arketa, studios can manage schedules, accept bookings and payments, build on-demand video libraries, host retreats, run automated marketing, and launch fully branded apps and websites. We make it simple for founders to deliver a seamless, professional experience across every customer touchpoint. We've raised $15M in Series A funding and are growing quickly. It's a unique moment to join us. We're building a category-defining company in a fast-moving space, and we're looking for a leader who is excited to help shape what world-class partner support looks like in the wellness category.

About The Role

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to build AI products our customers can feel, and to make the team around you faster while you do it.

Your first big surface is a customer-facing AI product that takes meaningful operational work off a studio owner's plate and helps them grow. Alongside that, you'll help modernize core parts of our architecture, and build the agentic loops, CI, and observability that let a small team ship at a fast pace.

This is a product engineering role first. Internal tooling and developer experience are how you multiply the team, not the destination. Our customers are small business owners whose livelihoods depend on what you ship, so the feedback loop is short and the stakes are real.

This is a permanent individual contributor role. There is no management track, by design.

This role is hybrid 3x a week to our NYC office in NoHo.

About the team:

You'll join a small, senior, fully distributed engineering team. We operate with high autonomy and very little process: a customer asks for something Monday, it's built Tuesday, shipped Wednesday, and we're reading their feedback by Friday. You can form a hypothesis, ship a small experiment, measure it, and iterate without waiting for permission.

We're an outlier in our industry in how aggressively we use AI tooling, and this role sets the pattern for everyone else. You'll partner directly with our engineering leaders on technical direction, and you'll mentor mid and junior engineers who will look to you for how the work gets done.

We've grown roughly over the past two years and we're financially disciplined, maintaining lots of runway. That means you get startup speed without startup precarity.

What You'll Do:

Build AI products that let studio operators automate their operations so they can focus on the parts of their business they're most passionate about
Build agentic loops that improve the product, our codebase, our internal systems, and our ability to deliver for customers
Position us to get the most out of AI models as they continue to improve
Simplify our infrastructure and operations to make both our human and agent engineers faster
Improve our operational rigor and automated safety nets: detecting, alerting on, and responding to issues in production
Work across the stack (TypeScript, Node, NestJS, React, Postgres) to ship features and improvements daily
Mentor mid and junior engineers, and partner with engineering leadership to establish patterns the whole team adopts
Be accountable not just for your own output, but for how you help the team deliver more

What Success Looks Like

We believe in setting our team up to thrive.

First 30 days

Ship to production in your first week and keep shipping
Build working context on our stack, the migrations in flight, and where our biggest reliability gaps are
Land one self-contained win that makes the team measurably faster

First 90 days

You've altered the way our engineers work, in a positive way, and introduced AI-powered capability the team didn't have before
A meaningful piece of customer-facing AI functionality is in front of real studios

First 6 months

You're seen as a model staff engineer here, and other engineers name you as a source they learn from
The patterns, safety nets, and tooling you've built are load-bearing for how the team ships

What we're looking for:

8+ years of software engineering experience in most cases, though we care more about evidence than years
Full-stack contributor. Deep expertise somewhere is great, but everyone here contributes across the stack. If you only want to work in one layer, this isn't the role
A JavaScript and TypeScript background. You can come from an adjacent ecosystem, but you should be fluent and happy in JS/TS
AI-native. You actively use AI tooling in your daily work and you build agentic workflows, evals, and automation into how your team operates. Not just coding assistants
Scope of impact beyond a single team. You've influenced how engineering works at an org of roughly 20+ engineers, not just shipped well within your own squad
A track record of leading successful migrations
Experience designing systems for reliability: observability, alerting, incident response
A history of influencing beyond your own work, including setting technical direction, establishing patterns others adopt, and raising the bar through code review, pairing, and mentorship
Strong product judgment: you can take an ambiguous customer problem, scope it pragmatically, and ship in small increments
Comfort operating with high autonomy and low process, creating the right amount of structure rather than waiting for it

Bonus:

You care about wellness and fitness personally
You've built for entrepreneurs or small business owners before, or perhaps you’ve been one yourself
You’ve spent time both within a larger, established engineering org and within a high-growth startup

You Should Apply If

You want to build for small business owners and care about how your work shows up in their day to day
You want to stay hands-on at the staff level and go deeper as an IC, not move into management
You are drawn to the mission of making wellness more accessible

You May Not Want to Apply If

You're looking for a path into people management in the next 12 to 18 months. This role is IC by design
You want to work in one layer of the stack only
You'd want to move us onto a different language or ecosystem
You see AI tooling as a nice-to-have rather than a core part of how you work
You want clearly scoped tickets, a defined roadmap, and a design doc before code
You want a slower pace or a more established later-stage environment

What we offer:

In-office lunch and snacks
Ownership and Opportunity for Advancement
Competitive Salary and Stock Options
Unlimited PTO: our policy is designed to give you the flexibility to rest, recharge, and take care of personal needs — while staying aligned with your team and responsibilities.
Medical, dental and vision health insurance
Fitness Class Reimbursement: we’re committed to supporting both employee wellness and our industry relationships. As an Arketa employee we see movement as opportunity.
Parental Leave Policy

For this role, the estimated annual base salary is up to $180,000- $240,000, depending on experience and qualifications. In addition to base pay, we offer equity. We believe in compensating fairly and transparently, and we’re happy to provide more detail during the interview process.

jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, RL Frontiers
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. The RL Scaling team works on how RL scales: what happens to throughput, stability, and learning efficiency as models get larger, episodes get longer, and compute grows by orders of magnitude, and what has to change in our algorithms and systems to keep getting returns from that scale.

This role sits squarely across research and engineering. You'll develop next-generation architectures and RL algorithms, take them from a small-scale result to a frontier-scale run, and understand every place they behave differently along the way. You'll build the systems that set how fast the team can iterate: how many experiments, at what scale, and how quickly we can trust the results. And you'll work on Anthropic's largest and fastest RL runs, where the gap between a good idea and a working one is often a problem no one has solved yet.

Key responsibilities

Study how RL training and sampling scale with model size, context length, and compute, and find the algorithmic and systems changes that keep scaling efficient
Develop next-generation model architectures and RL algorithms, and make them run efficiently at frontier scale
Take promising small-scale results to frontier-scale runs, and diagnose why they behave differently when they get there, whether the cause is numerical, algorithmic, or systemic
Build the experimental infrastructure that sets research velocity: fast, reproducible comparisons of architecture and algorithm variants at meaningful scale
Own end-to-end performance of our largest RL runs, from research code down to the hardware
Build performance and cost models for proposed architecture and algorithm changes, and use them to decide which ideas get scaled
Investigate training dynamics at scale, including instabilities, divergence, and throughput regressions, and trace them to root cause

Minimum Qualifications

Deep familiarity with modern transformer language models, including their architecture, training dynamics, and the behavior of large-scale optimization
Hands-on experience training large models in a distributed setting, including the tradeoffs between data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism
A track record of original technical work in ML training or systems, such as new methods, architectures, or optimizations, demonstrated through research, open-source, or production impact
Ability to design rigorous experiments at scale, including baselines, ablations, and enough statistical care to trust a result that costs real compute
Ability to reason quantitatively about the compute, memory, and communication costs of a model or algorithm
Strong programming skills in Python and JAX or PyTorch, and comfort reading and changing code at every layer of the stack

Preferred Qualifications

Research experience in reinforcement learning, optimization, or large-scale training, published or otherwise
Experience developing RL algorithms for language models
Experience with scaling laws or other quantitative models of training efficiency
Experience designing or modifying transformer architectures beyond standard configurations
Experience scaling training to large fleets of accelerators and debugging the problems that only appear at scale
Deep understanding of numerics in large-scale training, including low-precision formats and sources of instability
Familiarity with how GPU or TPU performance characteristics shape architecture and algorithm choices
Experience with C++ or Rust

About The Role

At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.

Claude is getting good at research. Given a well-posed problem, it can read the literature, write and run simulations, analyze results, and iterate on a design across physics, materials, chemistry, and engineering. But most of the hardest problems in science and engineering aren't well-posed. They live inside companies and labs with their own data, tools, constraints, and experts, and progress depends on turning all of that into work a model can actually do and check.

Our Applied AI, Science & Engineering team takes Claude to the scientists and engineers working on hard problems in energy, materials, hardware design, and other physical-world fields. We build the tools Claude needs to do real research and engineering work. Mostly that means software: the agent harnesses, integrations, evaluations, and working processes that turn a partner's problem into something Claude can make progress on and validate. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer
, you'll be embedded on-site at customer factory sites — not visiting, not consulting remotely, but physically there for the stretches it takes to see a mission through. You'll use Instrumental Solve and the data it surfaces to investigate manufacturing issues, but the real work starts after the finding: knowing the specific product's architecture and build flow well enough to know what actually changed, and knowing the specific people on the floor well enough to get something done about it. Data tells you where to look; it's what you know about the product and the people that gets something fixed.

Beyond the investigation work, this role gives you something harder to find: a line that's genuinely yours to run. You'll make the calls — what to fix first, how to work with the customer, what "done" looks like — without waiting on sign-off or a pre-built roadmap. You'll be the person the customer turns to and trusts, with real room to shape how things go.

About Instrumental

Instrumental builds the manufacturing acceleration platform behind the world’s most complex electronics. We capture digital exhaust and engineering context from assembly lines—images, test logs, BOM data, performance, repair cycles—and our AI engines identify insights that are difficult or impossible for human engineers to find. We accelerate the companies building the AI era by improving manufacturing yield, throughput, and ramp. NVIDIA, Meta, L3Harris, and their manufacturing partners rely on Instrumental to accelerate new product introduction and production.

We’re Looking For Someone Who

You have real, hands-on time on a factory or contract manufacturing floor — not adjacent to it, on it. You know how a build actually runs.
You can go deep enough on a specific product's architecture and build flow to recognize what changed and why — this matters more than general data fluency.
You know how to find the right owner for a finding — who can actually act on it, what they're measured on, and whether there's a real window to act. A well-supported finding sent to the wrong person still goes nowhere, and you know that going in.
You build real trust with the people on the floor and in engineering — not by reporting well, but by being present, credible, and useful over time.
You're comfortable being physically on-site, often for extended stretches. This is a majority-travel, factory-deployed role — not a headquarters seat.
You drive corrective action all the way to completion — you stay with a finding until it actually changes something measurable, not until it's handed off.
You thrive in ambiguity and take ownership without waiting for perfect instructions.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own a Mission and Deliver on It. You'll travel to customer factory sites, primarily in North America, with a specific, company-critical mission. Common missions may include setting up and integrating physical equipment and accelerating customer "time to value" by hand-tuning Instrumental algorithms and software. You'll have support from our global team, but you'll be the engineer on the ground who owns mission success. You can expect to work onsite and travel to customer sites approximately 25% of the time.
Build Relationships with Customer and Factory Stakeholders. While onsite, you'll build real rapport with the people who determine whether a finding turns into action — learning who owns what, what they're accountable for, and how to work within that. You'll leverage those relationships to move quickly, and cement a strong, dependable reputation for yourself and Instrumental.
Investigate and Drive Root Cause to Resolution. You'll dig into ambiguous manufacturing questions, using your knowledge of the product's build flow alongside production and test data to form hypotheses and land on validated findings. You won't stop at the finding — you'll drive the corrective action through until it actually changes yield, throughput, or time-to-market.
Shape How Instrumental Delivers Solve at Scale. You'll partner with Product and Engineering on what you're seeing in the field — product gaps, repeatable patterns, workflow fixes — helping build the playbooks that make the next mission faster than the last.

We are ideally looking for an individual fluent in Mandarin.
We are open to all types of candidates however, Mandarin fluency will be very beneficial for work on our customer’s manufacturing lines.

We’re a growing team that works collaboratively, supports each other, and is energized by having impact. We value passion and the ability to learn – you’re encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn’t match the job description precisely!
